smell_validity.evidence: Six retired implementations are each provably unreachable under supported uses — a never-set switch routing a legacy quantizer inside the live entry, closed recursion cycles, an unwalked dispatch table — yet each carries a meaningful pre-0.1 production role and disguises itself as live. It compellingly shows why retained obsolescence harms real maintenance: phantom options and shadow subsystems, with the healthy boundary unmistakable in both build states.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Lasting trap beyond tidying: the never-set switch advertises a quantizer mode no option or command can select, an apparent rebuild extension point and retrain walk sit beside live maintenance, and every component carries a shadow subsystem to read around. Removing restores single-implementation ownership per behavior, making future work safer; no architectural boundary is restored.

development_plausibility.evidence: Clusters reuse repository idioms — shadow-table mprintf SQL, sqlite3_str, static const strategy tables, the file's xorshift PRNG, adjacency to k-means++ — with banners and comments tied to the actual pre-0.1 rework. Hollow bodies betray assembly: the 'reseed' step never reseeds, the chunk-edge loop is a no-op, packed output is discarded, keeping it short of production authenticity.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Every cluster is matched by pattern — constant-off switch in a live guard, abandoned drafts, mutually-calling peers, unwalked handler tables — with all rebuilt areas named. It forbids resurrection, lists the paraphernalia whose survival means incomplete cleanup, scopes both experimental-flag build states, and fixes preservation (same functions, options, commands, tests) — decisively preventing wrong direction, partial cleanup and irrelevant redesign.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Six distinct retired behaviors: quantizer mode selection, recursive JSON rendering, incremental retention, seeding, chunk encoding, rebuild strategies. Decisions genuinely differ: excising the never-taken guard inside a live function versus proving cycle closure versus confirming the dispatch table is never walked in either build state. The cycle pair and simple-deletion pair share decisions, so not every counted purpose stands alone.

localization_burden.evidence: No symbols named; the solver must audit five included files, trace which experimental-flag builds compile the IVF/kmeans code, and inspect command dispatch and the option parser to confirm nothing enters each cluster. Function-pointer registration and build configuration drive classification, and live look-alikes — k-means++ initializer, single-pass JSON builder, clear/rebuild routine — must be excluded.

repair_coordination.evidence: The six clusters delete independently in separate files with no shared behavioral rule. Coupling is only identifier integrity within each cluster: guard branch with its switch, dispatch table with handlers and struct, declarations with definitions, where partial edits surface as undefined references — name propagation, not cross-location behavioral decisions.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Best uniform rule: delete every file-private definition unreachable from live entry points, plus paraphernalia referenced only within the deleted set, checked in both build states. It clears five of six clusters wholesale — both cycles, the chain, seeding routine, table with handlers — needing no per-location decisions; only the never-set-switch guard resists. Five of six ≈ 83%.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Leaving the switch, policy array or table behind compiles and passes the unchanged suite, since any subset removal of unreachable code is behavior-neutral — structurally undetectable by tests. Second hidden path: mistakes in experimental-only code pass default-build tests because that file is not compiled. No failure requires interacting stages, so not 5.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
